entries.name: Parahoric reduction theory of formal connections (or Higgs fields)
entries.abstract: In this paper, we establish the parahoric reduction theory of formal connections (or Higgs fields) on a formal principal bundle with parahoric structures. This generalizes the reduction theory due to Hukuhara-Levelt-Turrittin and Babbitt-Varadarajan in the case without parahoric structures [7], and Boalch's result in the case of regular singularity [14]. As applications, we first prove that a formal connection is intrinsically regular if and only if it is a parahoric formal connection, in combination with the works of Bremer-Sage [45] and Chen-Kamgarpour [20], providing various criteria for the regularity of formal connections. We then introduce a notion of relative regularity for formal connections and give criterions. Finally, we demonstrate a parahoric version of Frenkel-Zhu's Borel reduction theorem of formal connections [33].

entries.name: Localisation for the second-order Beckmann problem: bimartingale couplings and leaf decompositions
entries.abstract: We develop a second-order localisation theory for optimal transport based on leaf decompositions and bimartingale couplings, which impose martingale constraints in opposite directions on complementary orthogonal subspaces. It provides a second-order analogue of the classical decomposition of optimal transport into transport rays and monotone couplings: transport rays are replaced by the leaves of the $1$-Lipschitz derivative map $Du$ of an optimal dual potential $u\in C^{1,1}(\mathbb R^n)$, while monotone couplings are replaced by bimartingale couplings. We apply this framework to the three-marginal optimal transport problem introduced by Bolbotowski and Bouchitté, whose relaxation is the second-order Beckmann problem. We characterise the existence of bimartingale couplings through a convex-concave order condition. This yields a generalisation of Strassen's theorem from convex order to the convex-concave setting. Equivalently, the dual problem associated with the second-order Beckmann problem admits an optimiser whose derivative is an isometry. For absolutely continuous measures with common barycentre, assuming the existence of an optimal plan with absolutely continuous third marginal, we prove that every optimal plan decomposes into a family of problems on the leaves of $Du$. On each leaf, all optimal plans are completely described by bimartingale couplings between the corresponding conditional measures. Without this absolute continuity assumption on the third marginal, we show that the leaf decomposition persists in a more general form: optimal plans are mixtures of plans concentrated on triples $(x,y,z)$ satisfying $x\in \mathcal{S}_1$, $y\in \mathcal{S}_2$, and $z\in \mathcal{S}_1\cap \mathcal{S}_2$, where $\mathcal{S}_1$ and $\mathcal{S}_2$ are neighbouring leaves of $Du$.

entries.name: A Generalization of Ramanujan's Sum over Finite Rings
entries.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a generalization of Ramanujan sums over finite rings and derive an explicit formula for these sums. These generalized Ramanujan sums coincide with the eigenvalues of the unitary Cayley graph $\mathrm{Cay}(R,R^{\times})$, as follows from Babai's result on Cayley graph spectra. This provides a useful approach to determining the spectrum of the unitary Cayley graph. Moreover, under a certain independence condition on the maximal left ideals, we show that our formula extends the classical formula for Ramanujan sums to finite rings.

entries.name: A Riemannian Generalization of Wilks' Lambda for Testing Differences Among Brain Connectomes
entries.abstract: Analysis of variance (ANOVA) for grouped samples whose observations take values in a space with nontrivial geometric structure, either a differentiable manifold or a non-Euclidean metric space, is a problem that has received attention in recent years. This paper is concerned with brain connectomes. Functional data analysis is another important motivation. Most of the literature relies on approaches that assume very little about the geometric structure. The most prominent example is Fréchet ANOVA, a method that is valid in metric spaces under relatively weak hypotheses. We argue that the generality of these approaches has a price in statistical power. We propose an ANOVA test on the space of symmetric positive definite matrices with the affine-invariant Riemannian metric that exploits features specific to that space. The test is not easy to generalize to other settings, but we show that there is a notable difference in power relative to Fréchet ANOVA. We show it theoretically, by characterizing the asymptotic behavior of both tests for alternatives close to the null hypothesis. We also show it in practice, by describing the specific consequences of that difference for the analysis of brain imaging studies whose design involves collecting samples at multiple sites.

entries.name: Explicit analytic functions defining the images of simple wave-front singularities
entries.abstract: We construct explicit main-analytic functions for the images of the standard maps associated with simple wave-front singularities of types $A$, $D$, and $E$. The construction uses resultants of explicitly specified pairs of one-variable polynomials whose coefficients are expressed directly in the target coordinates of the standard maps. For types $A$ and $D$, it recovers one-variable discriminant representations. Using this, we give direct proofs of sharp bounds on the number of preimages of the standard map for types $A$ and $D$. For each of the exceptional types $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$, there exists an additional square factor in the resultant. Removing this factor gives the corresponding main-analytic function.

entries.name: Homotopy exponents of polyhedral products
entries.abstract: We study Moore's conjecture and homotopy exponents for polyhedral products. For $(\underline{CA},\underline{A})^K$ where each $A_i$ is finite and has torsion-free homology, we prove that if $(\underline{CA},\underline{A})^K$ is rationally hyperbolic, then it has no homotopy exponent at any odd prime. Under the additional hypothesis $ΣA_i$ is homotopy equivalent to a finite-type wedge of simply-connected spheres, we show Moore's conjecture holds for $(\underline{CA},\underline{A})^K$. We also give criteria such that, for a large family of polyhedral join products, the associated polyhedral products are rationally hyperbolic, mod-$p^r$ hyperbolic for all but finitely many primes, and have no homotopy exponent at all but finitely many primes.

entries.name: Dynamic Programming without Contractivity
entries.abstract: Optimality results in dynamic programming are usually derived from contraction arguments, which require discounting or uniform bounds on termination times. We show that, in many useful settings, contractivity can be replaced by a simple global stability condition that requires no rate or uniformity. Under this condition and mild order-theoretic assumptions, we obtain existence of optimal policies, uniqueness of the value function as a solution to the Bellman equation, and convergence of value function iteration and of Howard and optimistic policy iteration. Applications include optimal stopping without discounting, where contraction methods can fail, and Bayesian sequential analysis.

entries.name: The Stability of the Backward Problem for Photoacoustic Imaging in Attenuating Media via Carleman Estimates
entries.abstract: This paper investigates the backward problem in time for photoacoustic tomography (PAT) in attenuating media. It is well-established that photoacoustic imaging in attenuating media can be accurately modeled by spatial fractional-order damping. This inverse problem is ill-posed in the sense of Hadamard. In this work, we construct a novel class of Carleman estimates independent of spatial variables, and by virtue of these estimates, we establish conditional stability estimates for this problem for the first time. Building upon this, we propose a Tikhonov-type regularization functional and derive its associated adjoint system. Furthermore, leveraging the established conditional stability results, we derive the convergence rate of the proposed regularization approach. Finally, we validate the effectiveness of our theoretical findings through extensive numerical experiments.

entries.name: Penalized hyperviscous Navier-Stokes flows: well-posedness, incompressible limit and sharp decay
entries.abstract: We study a three-dimensional Navier--Stokes system obtained by Temam's penalty method in the presence of a biharmonic viscosity: the pressure and the divergence constraint are replaced by the term $-\varepsilon^{-1}\nabla\,div\,u$, and the convection term is written in skew-symmetric form. We prove global well-posedness in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ and global regularity for data of arbitrary size in $H^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$, with bounds uniform in $\varepsilon$ and in time. For data in $L^1\cap L^2$, the energy decays like $t^{-3/2}$, with a constant independent of $\varepsilon$; for data in $L^1\cap H^2$, the first two derivatives decay at the corresponding heat rates. We identify the leading asymptotic profile and show that $t^{3/2}\|u(t)\|_{L^2}^2\toγ_\varepsilon(8πν)^{-3/2}|m_\infty|^2$, where $m_\infty$ is an asymptotic momentum and the explicit factor $γ_\varepsilon\in(\frac23,1)$ measures the energy removed by the penalization. Consequently, the decay rates are optimal in $L^1\cap H^2$ under an explicit non-degeneracy condition. Finally, as $\varepsilon\to0$, the solutions converge globally in time to those of the incompressible hyperviscous Navier--Stokes equations at the rate $\sqrt\varepsilon$, up to an explicit initial layer, and $-\varepsilon^{-1}div\,u$ converges to the pressure.

entries.name: Group action-stabilizer graph of group actions of a group on a set
entries.abstract: In this paper we introduce the group action-stabilizer graph $GAS(G)$ of a group $G$ on a set $X$. Its vertex set is the collection of all non-trivial group actions of $G$ on $X$, and two vertices $φ$ and $ψ$ are adjacent if and only if the normal subgroups $\bigcap_{x\in X} G_x^φ$ and $\bigcap_{x\in X} G_x^ψ$ of $G$ intersect non-trivially, where $G_x^φ$ and $G_x^ψ$ are the stabilizers of $x$ with respect to the actions $φ$ and $ψ$, respectively. We show that $GAS(G)$ is obtained from the intersection graph of those normal subgroups of $G$ that occur as kernels of actions on $X$ by replacing each vertex by a clique of twin vertices, and we characterize a special subgraph $gas(G)$ of $GAS(G)$ in which the vertex set contains the actions $φ$ of $G$ on $X$ such that the kernels $\bigcap_{x\in X} G_x^φ$ are distinct. We determine the number of group actions within some specific groups and find certain conditions under which $GAS(G)$ is equal to $gas(G)$. We also show that, for a finite nilpotent group $G$ with at least two prime divisors, $gas(G)$ is a derived graph exactly when $G$ is cyclic of order $p_1p_2$, $p_1p_2p_3$, $p_1^2p_2$ or $p_1^3p_2$, and its complement is a derived graph exactly when $G$ is cyclic of order $p_1p_2$, $p_1p_2p_3$, $p_1^2p_2$ or $p_1^2p_2^2$.

entries.name: Shifted-Binomial Coordinates of Dilated Binomial Polynomials: Multinomial Decimation and Arithmetic Structure
entries.abstract: For integers $m\ge2$ and $r\ge1$, let $d=m+r-1$ and consider the unique expansion \[ \binom{mn}{d}=\sum_{k=1}^{d+1}T_{m,r,k}\binom{n+k-1}{d}. \] By a standard multisection of a rational generating function, the coordinates are a residue-class subsequence of multinomial coefficients: \[ T_{m,r,k}=[x^{mk-1}](1+x+\cdots+x^{m-1})^{m+r}. \] From this representation we obtain the exact support, a counting interpretation by words by drops (Theorem~\ref{thm:drops}), a reflection criterion (the nonzero row is palindromic precisely when $r\equiv2\pmod m$), and log-concavity, hence unimodality, of the nonzero row. An integer-valued polynomial argument gives the universal divisor $m/\gcd(m,r-1)$ of each row, and a prime-adic computation of the fixed divisor of $\binom{mX}{d}$ gives the exact greatest common divisor of each row, a sharpness criterion, and a family of rows in which the universal divisor is arbitrarily far from sharp. We also obtain the row sum $m^{m+r-1}$, a Catalan-number specialization, and explicit coefficient arrays for $m=2,3,4,5$. The methods are finite differences, multisection of rational generating functions, and fixed divisors of integer-valued polynomials.

entries.name: Optimal convergence rates in homogenization of Monge-Ampère equations with periodic measures
entries.abstract: We establish optimal convergence rates in periodic homogenization of Monge--Ampère equations, allowing the microscopic measure to be singular or degenerate. Let $μ$ be a nonnegative $\mathbb Z^n$-periodic Borel measure with $μ(\mathbb T^n)=1$, and set $μ_\varepsilon(E)=\varepsilon^nμ(E/\varepsilon)$. On a bounded convex domain $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, let $u^\varepsilon$ and $u$ be the convex solutions of \[ \det D^2u^\varepsilon=F(x,x/\varepsilon)\,μ_\varepsilon,\qquad\det D^2u=\overline{F}(x) \] with the same Dirichlet data, where the coefficient $F$ is bounded, uniformly positive, and periodic in its second variable, and $\overline F(x)=\int_{\mathbb T^n}F(x,y)\,dμ(y)$. For $m=0,1$ and $0<α\leq1$, we prove \[ \|u^\varepsilon-u\|_{L^\infty(Ω)}\leq C\varepsilon^{m+α},\qquad \forall\,0<\varepsilon\leq1, \] provided that $u\in C^{m+2,α}(\overlineΩ)$ and $F(\cdot,y)\in C^{m,α}(\overlineΩ)$ uniformly in $y$. These exponents are optimal in their respective regularity scales, and the constant $C$ is independent of the distribution of the microscopic measure. In particular, the estimates include the optimal quadratic rate for general periodic measures. Our proof of the lower-order estimate ($m=0$) relies on uniform Lipschitz estimates for periodic correctors. For the higher-order estimate ($m=1$), we introduce a constrained Monge--Ampère problem that produces convex approximations with prescribed cell averages. This construction captures the cancellation in the third-order corrector expansion without uniform Hessian bounds for the correctors.

entries.name: Fully Deterministic Shallow Neural Networks with Localized Activations: Construction and Optimal Sobolev Approximation
entries.abstract: We construct fully deterministic finite-dimensional spaces for Sobolev approximation using shallow neural networks with a localized activation $σ$, either Gaussian or tanh-difference. For a bounded Lipschitz domain $Ω\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, and a prescribed regularity index $s>0$, the approximation space at frequency resolution $M$ is\[ V_M^Ω=\operatorname{span}\left\{ σ\!\left(\frac{ω_i\cdot x-b_{j,M}}{\varepsilon_M}\right): 1\le i\le J_M,\quad 1\le j\le K_{i,M} \right\}. \]All parameters are prescribed explicitly and independently of the target function. The offset cutoff depends on the direction and the domain, with an exterior margin tending to zero. The feature count satisfies $N_M=\sum_{i=1}^{J_M}K_{i,M}\asymp M^d$. For sufficiently large $M$, we construct a bounded linear operator $\mathcal A_M^Ω:H^s(Ω)\to V_M^Ω$ that achieves the optimal approximation rate \[ \|u-\mathcal A_M^Ωu\|_{H^m(Ω)} \le C N_M^{-(s-m)/d}\|u\|_{H^s(Ω)} \] for every $u\in H^s(Ω)$ and every integer $0\le m<s$. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions illustrate the approximation behavior in $L^2$ and $H^1$.

entries.name: Self-intersecting sections of polar actions on simply connected manifolds
entries.abstract: We construct a polar action of $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ on a closed simply connected $11$-manifold with a compact three-dimensional section that is not injectively immersed. The section is injective over the regular part and has two distinct local branches along a singular stratum. All isotropy groups are connected, and all orbits are simply connected. This gives a negative answer to the injectivity question raised by Grove and Ziller.

entries.name: Measure Theory in Convergence Spaces Part I: Sion-Carathéodory Extension in Net Convergence Groups
entries.abstract: We study extension of additive measures when the range carries a prescribed separated Abelian net convergence. On a $σ$-complete, lattice-$σ$-continuous pseudo-D-lattice, we prove an uncontrolled modular extension theorem using finite-response reflection, closed countable summation and uniform closure. Completeness is imposed only on the limit-stable hull of the source values. No topology, lattice order or positive control is required in its range. Modular interval identities, an order-null separation argument and two uniform transfer arguments construct the extension before establishing its normality. A separate relative lifting theorem combines this modular construction with a nonmodular Sasaki argument. Its cone conditions are verified for positive lattice-group values, lattice-normed groups, products and limit-stable subgroups. These verifications give explicit positive, dominated lattice-normed and topological corollaries. Uniqueness holds among all sigma-additive extensions to the generated domain. Sion's inner and outer nets exist in the original convergence and recover the extension there. For Boolean domains we retain the stronger identification with the full regulated splitting class and the finite-variation and finite-semivariation results.

entries.name: Pattern-dependent stability of binary exponential perturbations
entries.abstract: We study how the arrangement of binary frequency perturbations affects the stability of exponential systems on an interval of length one. For frequencies $λ_n=n+s_nδ$, with $s_n\in\{-1,+1\}$, we represent synthesis in Fourier coordinates by a shifted-sinc operator $N_{δ,s}$ and identify its Gram operator as $G_{δ,s}=N_{δ,s}^*N_{δ,s}$. The optimal squared synthesis bounds are $1\pmρ_{δ,s}$, where $ρ_{δ,s}=\|P_-T_{2δ}P_+\|$ measures the interaction between the two sign classes. Using the finite-matrix representation of periodic perturbations, we prove that, for each fixed $0\leqδ<1/2$, the minimum lower bound among $p$-periodic binary patterns converges to the worst binary lower bound as $p\to\infty$. At Kadec's critical amplitude $δ=1/4$, the alternating pattern has a positive lower bound, whereas a step pattern reduces to a half-shifted Hilbert matrix and has lower bound zero. Every fixed periodic pattern nevertheless remains a Riesz basis. We discuss the resulting periodic extremal questions and record a direct perturbation estimate giving explicit stability neighborhoods around stable reference patterns.

entries.name: Banach-Cesaro positive operator-valued measure
entries.abstract: We construct a family of bounded, finitely additive, covariant positive operator-valued measures (POVMs) on the real line by applying generalised Banach-Cesaro asymptotic averaging to locally finite covariant POVMs. In contrast to the strictly shift-invariant case, where countably additive operator measures are restricted to scalar multiples of a single fixed operator, the introduced covariant setting allows for non-commuting averaged operator values while successfully normalising the total mass. We develop an integration theory for complex-valued functions by taking the completion of simple integrable functions with respect to the continuous operator norm induced by the positive integral of their absolute values. The integration spaces for the original and the averaged measures are shown to possess distinct null classes. Finally, we introduce the operator-valued Fourier transform on these integration spaces and analyze the core algebraic constraints imposed by the covariance property on the exponential multipliers.

entries.name: Bounding the security of the Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash function
entries.abstract: The Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash functions are a family of Cayley hash functions indexed by an integer parameter $k\ge 2$. Hashes are matrices in $SL_2(p)$ where $p$ is a large prime. We present an attack which finds collisions of length $O(\log p)$ whose average-case time complexity is $O(p^{0.28})$ when $k=2$ and $O(p^{0.36})$ when $k=3$ under an assumption in the spirit of Zaremba's Conjecture on continued fractions. This is an improvement on the more general attacks of Mullan-Tsaban and Slaughter which have average-case time complexity $O(\sqrt{p})$. For any $k$, the average-case time complexity of our attack is $O(p^{1-δ_k+o(1)})$ where $δ_k$ is the Hausdorff dimension of a certain Cantor set. This tends to $O(\sqrt{p})$ as $k\to\infty$, so our attack has time complexity comparable to Mullan-Tsaban and Slaughter's attacks as $k$ grows. We give examples of collisions for large primes found by our attack when $k=2, 3$.

entries.name: The bias interval of the elephant random walk
entries.abstract: Guérin, Laulin, Raschel, and Simon conjectured that the initial biases giving the superdiffusive elephant random walk a bimodal limit law form an interval centered at one half, and they described the problem as challenging. We prove this. For every superdiffusive memory the limit density has two local maxima exactly when the bias lies in a proper open interval, and outside it, including its endpoints, the density has a unique local maximum. The interval is nonempty exactly above a single memory threshold, numerically about $0.6688$. Near this threshold $a_*$ the distance between the two modes is of order $(a-a_*)^{1/2}$, and the width of the interval is of order $(a-a_*)^{3/2}$. The bias boundary is continuous and tends to zero at least quadratically fast as memory tends to one. The proof bounds the sign changes of the first and second differences of the finite walk, including those created at the boundary, and passes them to the limit.

entries.name: Fixed-space indices and symmetry breaking in variational problems
entries.abstract: We establish a quantitative criterion for variational bifurcation with prescribed exact stabilizers under finite group actions. Combining ordinary spectral flow on fixed-point spaces with minimal-overgroup nullities, we obtain a lower bound on the number of exact-stabilizer bifurcation parameters when the restricted singular set is finite. The theorem allows strongly indefinite Fredholm Hessians and requires endpoint invertibility only on the chosen fixed space, without parameter differentiability or regular crossings. When the restricted Hessians have finite Morse index, the criterion involves only indices and nullities. We also treat varying form domains under explicit transport assumptions and regular matrix Sturm--Liouville systems. As our principal application, we consider a Newtonian nine-body family consisting of two interlaced squares with fixed satellite masses and a varying central mass. We prove analytically that central configurations with two nonconjugate exact reflection stabilizers bifurcate at a common mass in $(142,150)$, displacing the central body from the centre of mass. The family contains a reported counterexample to Moeckel's linear-stability conjecture; our bifurcation proof is independent of that stability assertion.

entries.name: On the Cauchy problem for $σ$-evolution equations with time-dependent coefficients via upper decay indicators
entries.abstract: In this paper, the first main goal is to investigate the Cauchy problem for the linear $σ$-evolution equation $$ u_{tt}+a^2(t)(-Δ)^σu+b(t)u_t+m^2(t)u=0, $$ where propagation speed, damping term and mass are time-dependent functions. Under suitable assumptions on the interaction among these coefficients, we not only derive decay estimates for the solution and its derivatives in terms of the effective parabolic time scale $\mathcal{V}_{a,b}(s,t):=\int_s^t a^2(τ)/b(τ) dτ$, but also conclude the additional decay induced by the mass term and the upper decay indicators of the initial data. Especially, one can recognize that the time-derivative estimate for solutions exhibits a competition between $m^2(t)$ and $a^2(t)\left(1+\mathcal{V}_{a,b}(0,t)\right)^{-1}$. For the corresponding semi-linear problem with the nonlinear term $|u|^p$, we also establish global (in time) existence of small data solutions fulfilling decay estimates, coming from the mass factor $\exp\left(-\int_0^t m^2(τ)/b(τ)dτ\right)$, under the same assumptions on these coefficients.

entries.name: Unboundedness of regular del Pezzo surfaces over imperfect fields
entries.abstract: Over an F-finite field, regular del Pezzo surfaces are bounded. Over a non-F-finite field of characteristic two or three, regular del Pezzo surfaces are unbounded.

entries.name: A constructive inverse for the Jordan--von Neumann operator on abelian groups
entries.abstract: For an abelian group $G$ and a real Banach space $X$, we study the inhomogeneous Jordan--von Neumann equation $\mathsf{Q}[f] = g$, where $\mathsf{Q}$ is the quadratic difference operator of the parallelogram law. We characterize the functions $g$ in the image of $\mathsf{Q}$ and, under a summability hypothesis, recover a solution explicitly by an iteration on the diagonal followed by a propagation argument; neither regularity of $g$ nor divisibility of $G$ is required. As a consequence we obtain a sharp stability estimate of Forti--Găvruţa type for the quadratic functional equation.

entries.name: From two heptagrams to a 449-vertex 5-chromatic unit-distance graph
entries.abstract: We construct a 5-chromatic unit-distance graph on 449 vertices. Previously, the smallest known 5-chromatic unit-distance graph had 509 vertices. Our graph is a subgraph of a graph obtained by a simple greedy construction applied to a 14-vertex seed graph consisting of two heptagrams.

entries.name: Nonlinear Moments as Equivalence Classes: A Lyapunov-Perron Approach to the Invariance Equation
entries.abstract: The linear moment is well defined whenever the system and the exosystem have disjoint spectra. Its nonlinear counterpart is not: the existence and uniqueness of solutions to the invariance equation that defines it are in general not guaranteed, so additional assumptions such as Poisson stability of the exosystem and the exponential stability of the system are required to define the nonlinear moment. This paper reduces this asymmetry. By using the Lyapunov--Perron fixed-point argument, we show that under a condition called the strip condition, there exist local $\mathcal C^N$ solutions, with $N$ determined by the system and the exosystem, and every pair of $\mathcal C^1$ solutions has contact of order $k^-$, where $k$ is a spectral ratio determined by the system and the exosystem; the solutions are flat-equivalent when $k=\infty$. Based on this observation, we extend the concept of nonlinear moment as an equivalence class of functions rather than a function. The polynomial of degree $N$ or formal power series ansatz of the invariance equation are the distinguished representatives of the equivalence class. We also show that, when the system is exponentially stable, the moment describes the output shared by all trajectories up to the order $k^-$, which gives the moment a time-domain interpretation when the steady-state interpretation is not available. Finally, we show that the concept of moment matching also naturally extends as the definition of nonlinear moment is extended to an equivalence class. The ansatz also plays a crucial role in the extended notion of moment matching. The results are illustrated by a numerical example.

entries.name: Global well-posedness and scattering for the fractional inhomogeneous nonlinear Schrodinger equation with time-dependent damping
entries.abstract: In this paper, we prove the global well-posedness and scattering of solutions for a nonlinear Schrodinger type equation with fractional Laplacian, inhomogeneous nonlinearity and time-dependent damping.We give an elementary proof based on Strichartz estimates combined with estimates of the nonlinear term in mixed-norm spaces. To avoid the loss of regularity in the Strichartz estimates, we consider the radial data.

entries.name: Mechanism Design under Belief Disagreement: Allocation Flexibility and Rent Capacity
entries.abstract: A seller jointly chooses allocation and payments when buyers misperceive competition. Under independent private values, statewise participation, and payment restrictions, allocation determines both required rents and their delivery capacity. We separate these effects under a common subjective law. For three values and shared-top beliefs, explicit score and capacity conditions characterize globally optimal lower-value lotteries, including top-rent overflow and welfare differences among revenue optima. A two-buyer construction establishes a strict allocation advantage over every reserve under the same fixed reporting certificate and positive margin. A transport test and exact band-boundary incentive equalities identify separate conditions restoring objective-law revenue ceilings. For three bands and a common affine belief interval, an explicitly certified reserve attains the ceiling under stated score conditions. A case scaled to public collectible-auction records yields a nominal shared-top allocation gain of 24.72 cents per auction. A one-cent report-by-report margin yields matched gains of 1.48 cents under projection and 3.32 cents under shared-top beliefs; the three-band point-belief gain of 2.50 cents disappears with common-interval protection. These comparisons bound the additional recurring costs an allocation redesign can cover at the specified reporting requirement.

entries.name: Stepanov's method and uniform sumset estimates in arbitrary finite fields
entries.abstract: Let $A<\mathbb F_q^\times$ be a proper multiplicative subgroup that generates $\mathbb F_q$ over its prime field. We prove that \[ |A+A|\ge \tfrac18|A|^{3/2} \] whenever $|A|<q^{2/3}$, uniformly in the characteristic and extension degree, without quantitative restrictions on intersections with proper subfields. Moreover, in contrast with what is expected in prime fields, we show that no uniform bound with exponent larger than $5/3$ holds in $\mathbb F_q$ even for $|A| \approx q^{1/2}$. The proof's key idea is to run the prime-field Stepanov method in reverse, constructing an auxiliary polynomial whose specialization vanishes identically instead of requiring it to be nonzero.

entries.name: Data-driven discovery of sparse governing equations with parameterized operators
entries.abstract: We study parameterized SINDy (pSINDy), an extension of the Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) framework for the discovery of parsimonious governing equations involving operators with unknown parameters such as fractional-order Caputo derivatives, fractional Laplacians, and parameterized kernel operators. The framework jointly identifies the unknown operator parameters and sparse library coefficients through a sparsity-promoting optimization problem. To solve this problem, we develop and analyze the parameterized sequentially thresholded least-squares (pSTLSQ) algorithm. In each iteration, it removes terms with small coefficients, updates the operator parameters by a fixed number of optimization steps that improve the fit of the remaining library terms, and refits their coefficients by least squares. Under suitable assumptions, we prove that pSTLSQ converges locally to a local minimizer and give sufficient conditions for identifying the terms present in the governing equation. Numerical experiments demonstrate recovery of governing equations from noisy synthetic data for fractional ODEs, fractional PDEs, and nonlocal diffusion equations. We also examine the influence of the hyperparameters, discretization scheme, and noise, and compare pSTLSQ with two benchmark methods. All three methods identify the correct terms at low noise levels, but differ in parameter accuracy, cost, and sensitivity to initialization and the candidate library.

entries.name: A hybrid high-order discretization of a volume integral formulation for eddy currents on unstructured polyhedral meshes
entries.abstract: Volume integral formulations are attractive for eddy-current simulation because they require a mesh only of the conducting region. However, their dense interaction matrices make it important to control the number of unknowns needed for a prescribed accuracy. We propose an arbitrary-order Hybrid High-Order discretization of a current-based volume integral formulation on general unstructured polyhedral meshes. The method combines high-order polynomial approximation with local mesh refinement around defects and material interfaces. For bounded positive spatially varying resistivity and magnetic permeability uniform throughout space, we establish well-posedness and a priori error estimates using a constructive right inverse of the discrete divergence. Numerical experiments demonstrate convergence for smooth solutions and compare mesh refinement with increasing the polynomial degree. Selected comparisons show that higher degree on coarser meshes can reduce the number of current unknowns coupled by the Green operator and the associated storage for a prescribed accuracy. Finally, a three-dimensional eddy-current testing benchmark assesses the predicted impedance against experimental measurements, using local refinement around a narrow slot and reusing the system matrix and its factorization throughout the probe scan.

entries.name: Regularization for the inhomogeneous nonlinear Schrödinger equation in one dimension
entries.abstract: In this work, we investigate the initial data problem for the following inhomogeneous nonlinear Schrödinger (INLS) equation $$ i \partial_t u + \partial_x^2 u = \pm |x|^{-b} |u|^{2k} u, \quad u(0, x)= u_0(x),$$ where $b>0$ and $k\in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$. The singular potential $|x|^{-b}$ impairs the Sobolev regularity that can be propagated by the flow. We establish the regularization mechanism of this model and prove local well-posedness in $H_x^α$ for $α=5/2-b-$. Moreover, at the endpoint space $H_x^{5/2-b}$, we show that there is no $C^{2k+1}$ flow map at the origin. The proof combines the one-dimensional local smoothing effect with a normal-form reduction for the high-low interaction generated by the singular part of the coefficient. The argument applies to both the focusing and defocusing cases.

entries.name: The Schürmann-Vallentin lattice $\mathsf{L}_6^{c}$ gives the thinnest lattice sphere covering in dimension six
entries.abstract: We prove that the lattice $\mathsf{L}_6^{c}$ discovered by Schürmann and Vallentin in 2006 is the unique (up to similarity) six-dimensional lattice that gives the thinnest lattice sphere covering.

entries.name: Superintegrable Systems and the Tractor Connection
entries.abstract: Quadratic constants of motion for natural pseudo-Riemannian Hamiltonians with potential correspond to conformal Killing tensors admitting multiple Killing scales. Taking this correspondence further, we develop a dimension-independent ($n\ge 3$) framework for studying second-order superintegrable systems using conformal tractor calculus, and invariant BGG prolongation of the rank two conformal Killing equation. We apply this framework to classify second-order maximally superintegrable systems within certain natural families of Hamiltonians generated by pairs of conformally related Einstein metrics in arbitrary dimensions. We recover the second-order analogue of Bertrand's theorem as a special case.

entries.name: Jointly Recovering Destination Attractiveness and Spatial Preference Segments from Observed Tours via Inverse Optimization
entries.abstract: Quantifying destination attractiveness by counting visitors, the most direct approach, can favor accessible sites and understate destinations that travelers reach at considerable cost. Preferences may also cut across a priori socio-demographic groupings. This study develops an inverse optimization framework that recovers destination attractiveness and preference segments jointly from observed multi-stop trip tours and generalized travel costs, without prespecifying tour-level segment assignments or imposing a parametric distribution on the unexplained part of utility. Representing each destination visit as a link in an extended network turns utility-maximizing tour choice into an inverse shortest paths problem. We apply the framework to 2,931 holiday vehicle trip tours over 51 target municipalities in Hokkaido, Japan. Constraint generation and alternating optimization make estimation tractable in this multi-destination setting, and the segments recovered under a three-segment specification show contrasting spatial preferences across the established coastal centers, the corridor around Sapporo, and the inland lake districts. The recovered values are expressed on a common monetary scale across destinations and segments without segment-specific scale normalization. They are uncorrelated with visit counts in the input data (r = -0.01) yet moderately correlated with tourist arrivals from an independent prefectural survey (r = 0.40), and are positively associated with the cost of reaching a destination (r = 0.60); destinations above this cost-value relationship include niche places that visit counts alone do not distinguish. The results provide a spatially explicit account of destination value and preference heterogeneity that can inform urban and regional planning and segment-targeted marketing.

entries.name: Geometrising discrete representations in \(\textnormal{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})\)
entries.abstract: We prove the Deroin--Tholozan conjecture for discrete representations into \(\textnormal{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})\). More precisely, we give a complete characterisation of those representations of a closed surface group with discrete image that arise as holonomies of branched hyperbolic structures. The proof combines a factorisation theorem of Rong for maps between Seifert fibred spaces with a local surgery that allows one to reinsert pinched handles while preserving the prescribed holonomy. As a consequence, we also obtain symmetric realisations on finite covers associated with normal torsion-free subgroups of the image.

entries.name: An ADMM-Based Approach to the Large-Scale Geomagnetically Induced Current Blocker Placement Problem
entries.abstract: We propose an Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM)-based approach for addressing the challenge of determining placements for geomagnetically induced current (GIC) blocking devices on large-scale transmission networks. Traditional formulations of this placement problem lead to mixed-integer nonlinear programs (MINLPs) that are difficult for state-of-the-art MINLP solvers, which often struggle to exploit problem structure and fail to produce high-quality solutions on large systems. To overcome these challenges, the proposed method employs a three-block ADMM decomposition enhanced with (i) partial linearization of the GIC-related nonlinearities, supported by conditions guaranteeing exactness, and (ii) heterogeneous penalty parameters that significantly accelerate convergence to high-quality local solutions. Numerical experiments on newly constructed large-scale benchmark systems (up to 10,000 buses) demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods by several orders of magnitude in runtime while producing solutions whose objective values closely approach the ideal all-blocker lower bound. These results highlight the effectiveness and scalability of the proposed approach for mitigation planning efforts in large transmission networks.

entries.name: The Gerards-Schrijver conjecture on the Edmonds-Johnson property is false
entries.abstract: An integral matrix $A$ has the Edmonds-Johnson property if, for all integral vectors $b,c,l,u$, the first Chvátal closure of $\{x: b\le Ax\le c,\ l\le x\le u\}$ equals its integer hull. Gerards and Schrijver conjectured that a totally half-modular matrix has the Edmonds-Johnson property if and only if it has no minor equal to one of two specific matrices, of size $3\times3$ and $3\times4$. We disprove this conjecture. We give a totally half-modular $5\times6$ matrix that does not have the Edmonds-Johnson property and has no minor equal to either matrix. It is a minimal obstruction: every proper minor has the Edmonds-Johnson property. The proofs work on a graph whose edges are the rows and bounds of the matrix, and on which the minor operations act by deleting, contracting and halving edges. For minimality, we reduce every proper minor to two classes of matrices known to have the Edmonds-Johnson property.

entries.name: Some attractive bases for the Onsager Lie algebra
entries.abstract: The Onsager Lie algebra $\mathcal{O}$ is defined by generators $A$, $B$ subject to the Dolan-Grady relations $[A,[A,[A,B]]] = 4[A,B]$ and $[B,[B,[B,A]]] = 4[B,A]$. It is known that $\mathcal{O}$ is infinite-dimensional. In this paper, we consider three bases for $\mathcal{O}$. The first basis was recently introduced by the author, and the second basis is a variation of the first. The third basis was introduced by Baseilhac and Crampé in 2019. By construction, the elements in each basis are recursively obtained from $A$, $B$. Using the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ loop algebra, we express every basis element in closed form. We then describe how these three bases are related to each other. Next, we consider a finite-dimensional irreducible $\mathcal{O}$-module $V$. Associated with $V$ are six well-known decompositions: the eigenspace decomposition of $A$ and the eigenspace decomposition of $B$, together with four other decompositions of $V$ said to be split. We show that on each decomposition, every element of the first two bases acts in a block diagonal, block upper bidiagonal, block lower bidiagonal, or block tridiagonal fashion. We illustrate these actions using a tetrahedron diagram. We also determine how the elements of the third basis act on the six decompositions. To obtain our results about finite-dimensional irreducible $\mathcal{O}$-modules, we use the theory of tridiagonal pairs.

entries.name: KAM theory for contact Hamiltonian systems
entries.abstract: In both finite and infinite dimensions, we establish the first frequency-preserving KAM theorems for full-dimensional Legendrian tori in contact Hamiltonian families with general analytic coupling between the momenta and the contact variable. After adjustment of external parameters, the flow on each torus is analytically conjugate in the original time to the prescribed translation, with estimates uniform as the damping parameter crosses zero. This coupling can generate nonzero mean damping at first order even when the damping parameter vanishes. In finite dimensions, nonzero mean damping yields a time-preserving analytic contact linearization near the torus. In both settings the invariant graphs give global analytic solutions of stationary Hamilton--Jacobi equations whose characteristic flows are conjugate to the prescribed translation. A novel consequence in finite dimensions is that, under global Tonelli assumptions and strict increase in the contact variable, this analytic solution is both the unique forward and the unique backward weak KAM solution, and its associated Legendrian graph is an invariant torus carrying quasi-periodic dynamics.

entries.name: Spectral radii of connected graphs with prescribed maximum degree
entries.abstract: For a real number $α>0$ and a positive integer $r$, we give recursive characterizations of the existence of finite simple connected graphs $G$ with adjacency spectral radius $ρ(G)=α$ and maximum degree $Δ(G)\le r$ (or $=r$). Adding one vertex to a graph $F$ at a time to update the Schur-complement $q=α-{\mathbf b}^{\mathsf T}B^{-1}{\mathbf b}$, where $B=αI-A(F)$ is positive definite and ${\mathbf b}$ is a nonzero $0$--$1$ that specifies the neighbours of $z$ in $F$. Realizability is characterized by admissible constructions with positive intermediate outputs $q$ and a final zero output. We also establish a reduction for a graph $G$ obtained by attaching pairwise disjoint rooted trees, each by a single edge, to a nonempty connected graph $H$. Assume that $αI-A(T)\succ0$ for every attached tree $T$. For each $z\in V(H)$, let $q_{z,1},\ldots,q_{z,s_z}$ be the positive root pivots obtained by the scalar tree recursion for the trees attached to $z$, and set \[ a_z=α-\sum_{j=1}^{s_z}q_{z,j}^{-1}, \qquad M_H(\mathbf a)=\operatorname{diag}(a_z:z\in V(H))-A(H), \] where an empty sum is zero. Then $ρ(G)=α$ if and only if $M_H(\mathbf a)\succeq0$ and $\det M_H(\mathbf a)=0$. Taking $H=K_1$ recovers the tree criteria, while $δ(H)\geq2$ gives criteria for graphs with prescribed 2-core $H$. In particular, for unicyclic graphs of prescribed cycle length, path continuants reduce the spectral condition to positivity inequalities and one scalar equation.

entries.name: Multi-location Newsvendor: An Interpretable Inventory Policy
entries.abstract: We study a multilocation newsvendor problem in which inventory is chosen before demand is observed and surplus stock can subsequently be transshipped to locations with shortages. The objective is to minimize expected holding, backlog, and transportation costs over a metric network. Under uniform transportation costs, the optimality conditions balance local and aggregate demand coverage and reduce to a scalar search under mild regularity conditions. We use this structure to develop an interpretable iterative heuristic for general metrics. The heuristic calibrates effective transportation costs from lateral shipments under independent stocking and uses them to construct location-dependent pooling weights. These weights have a direct operational interpretation through the cost of serving demand at other locations. Under the stated assumptions, the heuristic recovers the exact uniform-metric solution. Numerical experiments on structured and random networks show costs close to the sampled optimum on average and substantial savings relative to independent stocking.

entries.name: The Curved Exponential Family of Cylindrical Distributions: m-Projection, Curvature and a Test of the von Mises-Fisher Component
entries.abstract: Cylindrical data pair a vector in R^d with a direction in S^(m-1). We study a family in which the direction is von Mises-Fisher and, given the direction, the vector is Gaussian with mean affine in it; this generalizes the Mardia-Sutton model. The family is a curved exponential family inside a regular family with Fisher-Bingham directions. We state necessary and sufficient conditions for the maximum-likelihood estimator to exist and be unique. The estimator is explicit except for one scalar root and is the m-projection (Kullback-Leibler projection) of the moment-matching member. Every moment it does not match is a function of one residual, the gap between the sample and fitted second moments of the direction. The squared length of this gap in the Fisher metric is the classical score test of von Mises-Fisher against Fisher-Bingham directions, due to Cox on the circle and extended by Mardia, Holmes and Kent. Specific here are this reading and the exact invariance of its law to the regression part. The exponential curvature lies only in the directions of the regression matrix. In closed form, the information lost on this matrix against the expected information is m-1 observations for uniform directions and (m+1)^2/(m-1) in the limit of high concentration; conditioning on the directions recovers it. Finite mixtures are identifiable. On buoy records the test rejects von Mises-Fisher directions, and generalized von Mises directions raise the held-out log-density by 0.45 nats per observation with one component.

entries.name: Deterministic regularisation of the nonsymmetric eigenproblem
entries.abstract: We give a deterministic algorithm for pseudospectral shattering in exact arithmetic. This resolves an important open problem in the complexity of the nonsymmetric eigenproblem. Given a complex contraction $A$ of order $n\ge2$ and $0<δ<1/2$, we compute a perturbation $E$ with $\|E\|<δ$ such that $A+E$ has simple spectrum. The ratio of its eigenbasis condition number to its minimum eigenvalue gap is at most $C(n/δ)^{20/3}$. The algorithm also computes an exact eigensystem of $A+E$. It uses $O(n^3\log^d(n/δ))$ real-field operations and comparisons, where $C$ and $d$ are absolute constants. We choose the rank-one perturbations using a lower bound on the circle mean of the logarithm of the discriminant modulus. A quadratic penalty controls how far the accumulated updates move the matrix. By using the same reference eigenbasis for several updates, we can estimate all the current projector norms while recovering only the directions needed for the next perturbation.

entries.name: Rank-unimodality of one-descent composition ideals
entries.abstract: The principal ideal of a composition consists of its distinct generalized subwords, ranked by the sum of their parts. We prove rank-unimodality for every composition with at most one descent and for every bitonic composition. Both the part sizes and the number of parts are unrestricted. The main ingredient is a coupling for a monotone host. If a subword is chosen uniformly among those of weight at most n, its length and its unused weight can be made to increase weakly when n increases by one. A decreasing threshold on the next available part then compares the positive difference of two ordinary rank coefficients with an earlier cumulative ratio. This supplies the coefficient inequality in the hereditary reduction at a strict peak.

entries.name: Neural Schrödinger Bridge via Yasue Action with Applications to Generative Modeling
entries.abstract: We propose a novel neural solver for inferring the continuous state evolution of the Schrödinger bridge problem. The proposed solver builds on a saddle point formulation involving the Yasue action functional. This allows us to realize the continuous state evolution by learning the optimal velocity for an ordinary differential equation, as opposed to learning the optimal drift for a stochastic differential equation. The proposed solver only uses the source and the target samples, and not the source and target distributions per se, which makes it particularly suitable for high dimensional applications arising in generative modeling. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed solver using several numerical experiments in low and high dimensions, using both real and synthetic datasets.

entries.name: Finsler--Sobolev inequalities: optimality & rigidity
entries.abstract: We establish optimal Sobolev and logarithmic-Sobolev inequalities on non-compact, possibly non-reversible Finsler manifolds with non-negative weighted Ricci curvature. The optimal constants exhibit no dependence on reversibility -- confirming Ohta's conjectural principle -- being governed solely by the forward and backward asymptotic volume ratios. We then apply the logarithmic-Sobolev inequality to establish the optimal hypercontractivity estimate for the heat flow in the same geometric setting. The equality cases of the above optimal inequalities imply strong rigidity in the underlying manifold, characterized by fine properties of the flag and $S$-curvatures as well as the precise profiles of the corresponding extremizers. We illustrate our results by examples including Randers metrics obtained by Zermelo navigation with Killing vector fields, and weighted convex cones in $\mathbb{R}^n$ endowed with arbitrary Minkowski norms, the latter showing that the forward and backward asymptotic volume ratios may differ.

entries.name: Nearly Minimax-Optimal Sample Complexity of Natural Policy Gradient with a Matching Information-Theoretic Lower Bound
entries.abstract: A fundamental question in reinforcement learning is how many sampled transitions are needed to learn a near-optimal policy, and whether direct policy optimization can attain this statistical limit. To answer this question, we consider natural policy gradient (NPG), a widely used policy optimization method. We study tabular finite-horizon Markov decision processes (MDPs) with known rewards and unknown horizon-dependent transition kernels, accessed through a generative model. Our sample-based NPG algorithms update the policy by backward sweeps and do not estimate transition probabilities. Under three different batch-size and step size schedules, we establish last-iterate guarantees with sample complexity $\widetilde O(SAH^4/\varepsilon^2)$, where $S$, $A$, and $H$ denote the number of states, the number of actions, and the horizon length, respectively. In this setting, horizon-dependent transition kernels contribute a factor of $H$ to our transition-query bound. Our information-theoretic lower bound of $Ω(SAH^4/\varepsilon^2)$ shows that the resulting $H^4$ dependence is unavoidable in the worst case, even for agents that select their queries adaptively. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first last-iterate guarantees for NPG whose sample complexity matches an information-theoretic lower bound up to logarithmic factors. Consequently, our results demonstrate that direct policy-space optimization through NPG can achieve the fundamental statistical limits of reinforcement learning while guaranteeing the performance of the final policy. Furthermore, for known kernels, we prove that exact NPG with a constant step size $η=1/H$ requires $Ω(H^2/\varepsilon)$ iterations in the worst case, matching the known upper bound for that step size.

entries.name: Strictness of the containment of Kirk's asymptotic contractions in a class defined by two quasi-metrics
entries.abstract: Kirk's asymptotic contractions are defined by moduli $ψ_n$ which converge uniformly on $[0,\infty)$ to a Boyd--Wong function and are evaluated at the distance $d(x,y)$ only. A relaxed class, in which the estimate involves a lower and an upper quasi-metric built from the four distances $d(x,y)$, $d(x,Ty)$, $d(Tx,y)$ and $d(Tx,Ty)$, was recently shown to contain Kirk's class and to admit the same fixed point conclusion. It was left open whether the containment is strict. We prove that it is. The separating maps form a family of radial damping maps $T(x)=λ(\norm{x})x$ on a normed space, where $λ\colon[0,\infty)\to[0,ρ]$ is continuous, $0\leρ<1$, nonconstant and periodic: every such map is a relaxed asymptotic contraction with explicit linear moduli, whereas its one-step dispersion at a fixed distance is unbounded, so that no finite Kirk modulus exists. A slowly modulated nonperiodic damping law is treated as well. We further show that strictness can occur only when the image $T(X)$ is not relatively compact: in a complete space, if $T(X)$ is relatively compact, the two classes coincide, hence on a compact (in particular finite) space no separating example exists. Applications to semi-active vibration isolation with amplitude-dependent damping and to digital maturity gaps in the digital transformation of small and medium-sized enterprises are discussed, and numerical illustrations are provided.

entries.name: The shortest figure-eight geodesics on random hyperbolic surfaces
entries.abstract: We consider primitive unoriented figure-eight geodesics on a closed hyperbolic surface of genus $g$ sampled from Weil--Petersson measure. The shortest of these geodesics realizes the non-simple systole. He, Shen, Wu and Xue proved that its length is tight after centering at $a_g=\log g-\log\log g$. We prove that, as $g\to\infty$, the point process of centered lengths converges to a Poisson process on $\mathbb R$ with intensity $e^s\,ds/(8π^2)$. Its first arrival gives a reflected Gumbel limit for the centered systole $M_g$. We also prove convergence of the marked process in which each figure-eight carries the three cuff lengths of its supporting pair of pants, normalized by their sum. In the limiting process, the third cuff accounts for half the perimeter. The two winding cuffs, ordered at random, divide the other half uniformly. These splits are independent across points and independent of the limiting lengths. Uniform exponential bounds on both tails of $M_g$ give convergence of all fixed polynomial moments. At the critical exponent $-1$, we obtain $\mathbb E_g e^{-M_g}\sim(\log g)/(16π^2)$.

entries.name: A two-sided continued-fraction criterion for the Erdős-Moser equation and Erdős's 1949 problem
entries.abstract: We give a two-sided continued-fraction criterion for the Erdős--Moser equation $1^k+2^k+\dots+(m-1)^k=m^k$. Writing $m=k/\log 2+3/2+γ_m/m$, Gallot, Moree and Zudilin showed that a solution yields a convergent of $\log 2/(2N)$, for a known divisor $N$ of $k$, followed by a large partial quotient. We show that an explicit two-sided estimate for $γ_m$, from our earlier centre-of-mass work, restricts this partial quotient, for each value of $\gcd(k/N,2m-3)$, to two consecutive values, or to three in the exceptional case that an integer lies in an explicit interval of relative length $O(1/m)$. This excludes the first index left open by their computation and, without extending their continued-fraction computation, raises the lower bound for a nontrivial solution from $m>2.71\cdot 10^{1667658416}$ to $m>6.26\cdot 10^{1667658425}$. The same criterion gives an effective form of the asymptotic results of Best and te Riele on Erdős's 1949 problem on the largest term of $1^n+\dots+(m-1)^n$. We determine all 50 pairs $(m,n)$ with $m<10^{399}$ for which $(m-2)^n<(m-1)^n/2$ and $1^n+\dots+(m-1)^n>m^n$; in particular, the smallest example found by Best and te Riele in 1976 is the smallest such pair, a question they had left open. For $n<0.69\cdot 10^{399}$ we also determine the 51 elements of O'Bryant's exceptional set $A_2$ and all 101 terms of OEIS A129935 below this bound, one of them not previously listed, and settle several conjectures recorded in the OEIS. Finally, using only the upper bound in our estimate for $γ_m$ and its positivity, we show that the second part of Erdős's problem, the existence of infinitely many such pairs, is equivalent to the infinitude of $A_2$ and to the existence of infinitely many even-index convergents $p_j/q_j$ of $\log 2$ with $p_j$ even, $q_j$ odd and $q_j(q_j\log 2-p_j)<Θ(q_j)$, where $Θ(q)=(\log 2)/3+O(q^{-2})$ is explicit.

entries.name: Finite-difference neural policy iteration for high-dimensional degenerate Hamilton--Jacobi equations
entries.abstract: We develop a finite-difference neural policy iteration method for high-dimensional degenerate Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman and Isaacs equations. Artificial viscosity yields a monotone finite-difference operator, and neural networks approximate the linear equations of semi-discrete policy iteration using local stencil values. This avoids global tensor-grid storage. For measurable feedbacks, we bound the propagation of evaluation, terminal, gradient, and control optimization errors by a geometrically weighted sum. Discrete comparison, consistency, and vanishing viscosity relate the approximation to the original degenerate equation. On coupled manufactured problems with rank-deficient diffusion, the method achieves lower mean errors than direct physics-informed neural networks at every tested dimension from five to fifty under equal training time. At fifty dimensions and $900$ seconds, the mean relative $L^2$ error over three paired seeds is about $40\%$ lower. Two-dimensional refinement attains $0.297\%$ error against the original degenerate solution, with independent grid references separating approximation error from viscosity bias. In a twenty-dimensional game with finite control sets, reusing policies reduces the measured time to a relative error of $5\%$ by $24.3\%$ compared with direct minimization of the same discrete residual with fresh samples at every update.

entries.name: Numerical approximation of the Hilfer fractional derivative using orthogonal Quasi-Polynomials
entries.abstract: A numerical approach based on a composite Gaussian quadrature for the Hilfer fractional derivative is presented. This approach employs quasi-polynomials that are orthogonal with respect to the weight function on the interval $(0,1)$. As special cases, the Riemann--Liouville and Caputo fractional derivatives are obtained. Error bounds for the approximation are derived. To confirm the convergence rates as well as the high efficiency of the new approach, numerical examples are provided.

entries.name: Inverse problems for ZS operators and their isomorphisms, II
entries.abstract: We study isomorphic inverse spectral problems for Zakharov--Shabat operators on the unit interval with generic boundary conditions. A unitary gauge transformation reduces these problems to the corresponding problems with basic boundary conditions, with an explicit shift of the spectral parameter. Using previous results for canonical boundary conditions and four-spectra data mapping we describe isomorphic inverse spectral problems for Zakharov--Shabat operators. Moreover, study other inverse problems including replacing mappings and canonical relations.

entries.name: Global existence and decay estimates for classical solutions to 2D compressible micropolar fluid equations with vacuum
entries.abstract: In this paper, we consider the Cauchy problem for the two-dimensional compressible micropolar fluid equations with far field vacuum. Under the assumption that the initial energy is sufficiently small, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of strong and classical solutions, allowing for large oscillations in the initial data. The key to the proof is to derive {\it a priori} decay estimates for the pressure, the velocity gradient, and the microrotational velocity, which enable us to close the bootstrap argument. We also handle the difficulties arising from the coupling between the velocity field and the microrotational velocity.

entries.name: Cayley Regression for Finite Groups with a Cyclic Subgroup of Index Two
entries.abstract: A finite group $G$ is a Cayley regression if every generalized Cayley graph of $G$ is isomorphic to a Cayley graph of $G$, and a $k$-Cayley regression if this holds for all such graphs of valency at most $k$. We show that the dihedral group $D_{2n}$, $n\geq2$, is a $2$-Cayley regression if and only if it is a $3$-Cayley regression, which holds exactly when $n$ is a prime power, and that for $k\geq4$ it is a $k$-Cayley regression if and only if $n$ is an odd prime power or $n\in\{2,4\}$. Groups with a cyclic subgroup of index two that are neither cyclic nor dihedral are not even $2$-Cayley regressions; consequently, a group with a cyclic subgroup of index two is a Cayley regression if and only if it is isomorphic to $C_2$, $C_4$, $C_6$, $C_{10}$, or $D_{2n}$ with $n$ as above. Finally, every split metacyclic group $C_m\rtimes C_q$ with $m>2$ and odd $q\geq3$ is not a $2$-Cayley regression.

entries.name: A $C_2$-cofinite non-rational principal $W$-algebra of type $D_4$
entries.abstract: We show that a simple principal $W$-algebra can be $C_2$-cofinite and non-rational. For $\mathcal W=\mathcal W_{-38/7}(D_4,f_{\mathrm{reg}})$ of central charge $-50$, D. Xie predicted seventeen irreducible modules and a logarithmic module of lowest conformal weight $-2$. We determine the Zhu algebra $A(\mathcal W)$ and the Poisson algebra $R_{\mathcal W}=\mathcal W/C_2(\mathcal W)$. Both have dimension $18$, and $A(\mathcal W)\cong\mathbb{C}^{16}\times\mathbb{C}[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)$. We construct all seventeen irreducible $\mathcal W$-modules using the realization of $\mathcal W$ as a diagonal coset in $L_{-14/3}(D_4)\otimes L_1(D_4)$ and our previous classification of irreducible $L_{-14/3}(D_4)$-modules in the category $\mathcal O$. We also construct an indecomposable $L_{-14/3}(D_4)$-module and use the coset realization to obtain an indecomposable logarithmic $\mathcal W$-module. Its lowest generalized $L(0)$-eigenspace is two-dimensional, and $L(0)$ acts on this space by a nontrivial Jordan block with eigenvalue $-2$.

entries.name: Quantitative Convergence of the Spherical Brownian Motion collisional particle system for the Maxwellian Landau Equation
entries.abstract: In this paper, we establish the quantitative convergence of the spherical Brownian motion (SBM) collisional particle system for the Maxwellian Landau equation via Wasserstein distances. When used as numerical method, it enjoys linear complexity $O(N)$ in particle number $N$, and conserves the momentum and energy almost surely. Moreover, only random grouping and sampling are needed for simulations without further numerical discretization. In the first part, we identify the large particle mean field limit of the system, and the Wasserstein convergence to the limit is justified through a coupling similar to the recent work for the Nanbu type Monte Carlo method \cite{BorghiPareschi2025}. The key difference is that the particles in our coupled shadow system are not i.i.d. due to the perfect matching. In the second part, the convergence of the mean field dynamics to the Landau solution is justified by the relative entropy with a bound $O(τ^2)$, being $τ$ the stepsize. This results in an $O(τ)$ bound for the Wasserstein distance error. A crucial technical tool in the convergence in relative entropy is to provide suitable bounds on the derivatives of the logarithmic density or score function in the mean field dynamics. The combination of these estimates leads to the full convergence of the squared Wasserstein distance with order $O(N^{-1/2}+τ^2)$ for the numerical scheme in $d=3$.

entries.name: Note on polychromatic coloring of hereditary hypergraph families III
entries.abstract: For every integer $h\ge4$ we construct a hereditary family of hypergraphs with $m_2=h$ and \[ m_3\ge 2(h-1)+2\left\lfloor\frac{h-1}{3}\right\rfloor+1 \approx \frac{8}{3}m_2. \] This improves the lower bound $m_3\ge 2m_2$ from the preceding notes for every $m_2\ge4$. We also show that the worst-case integrality gap of the weighted transversal problem over hereditary families with $m_2\le h$ is between $h-1$ and $5000h$. As a consequence, every such family admits strong $\varepsilon$-nets of size at most $5000h/\varepsilon$.

entries.name: Interface-aware dynamic mode decomposition with control for partitioned multiphysics systems
entries.abstract: We develop an interface-aware dynamic mode decomposition with control (DMDc) formulation for multiphysics systems, within an optimization-based partitioned coupling framework. The finite-element interface-input operator is projected onto the reduced space and kept fixed during identification, while the unknown state-dependent local dynamics are learned from trajectory data. The common interface control is recomputed online by minimizing the mismatch between the reconstructed physical interface quantities. The formulation accommodates local subproblems governed by ordinary differential equations (ODEs) and differential--algebraic equations (DAEs). For a DAE subproblem, tangent projection identifies the state dynamics, whereas a residualized normal regression identifies the pressure balance and provides an algebraic pressure reconstruction. We further propose regularized quadratic correction DMDc to enrich the tangent dynamics and, for DAEs, the normal pressure balance through jointly fitted linear and compact quadratic operators. Feature normalization and block-dependent regularization control the enlarged regression while retaining the prescribed interface operators and identified DAE geometry. The proposed framework is evaluated on problems involving both ODE--ODE and DAE--ODE couplings. The numerical results demonstrate accurate predictions and stable long-time behavior.

entries.name: Quadratic unitary Cayley graphs over finite commutative rings
entries.abstract: Let $R$ be a finite commutative ring with identity, and let $T_R=Q_R\cup(-Q_R)$, where $Q_R=\{u^2:u\in R^\times\}$. In this paper, we investigate the spectral properties of quadratic unitary Cayley graphs $\operatorname{Cay}(R,T_R)$, over finite commutative rings with identity. We determine all the eigenvalues of $\operatorname{Cay}(R,T_R)$ when $R$ has odd characteristic. Our results extend the previously known spectral formulas for this family of graphs. We also obtain all the eigenvalues when the characteristic of $R$ is $2$. Furthermore, for rings of odd characteristic, we give a complete characterization of when $\operatorname{Cay}(R,T_R)$ is a strongly regular Cayley graph.

entries.name: Sharp relations between volume growth, isoperimetry and escape probability in vertex-transitive graphs
entries.abstract: We prove sharp bounds on the probability that the simple random walk on a vertex-transitive graph escapes the ball of radius $r$ before returning to its starting point. In particular, this shows that if the ball of radius $r$ has size slightly greater than quadratic in $r$ then this probability is bounded from below. On the other hand, we show that if the ball of radius $r$ has volume slightly less than cubic in $r$ then this probability decays logarithmically for all larger balls. These results represent a finitary refinement of Varopoulos's theorem that a random walk on a vertex-transitive graph is recurrent if and only if the graph has at most quadratic volume growth. They also imply the existence of a gap at $0$ for escape probabilities: there exists a universal constant $c>0$ such that the random walk on an arbitrary vertex-transitive graph is either recurrent or has a probability of at least $c$ of escaping to infinity. We also prove versions of these results for finite graphs, in particular confirming and strengthening a conjecture of Benjamini and Kozma from 2002. Amongst other things, we also generalise our results to give a sharp finitary version of the characterisation of $p$-parabolic vertex-transitive graphs, prove a number of sharp isoperimetric inequalities for vertex-transitive graphs, and prove a locality result for the escape probability of the random walk on a vertex-transitive graph that can be seen as an analogue of Schramm's locality conjecture for the critical percolation probability.

entries.name: Super Guarding and Dark Rays in Art Galleries
entries.abstract: We explore an Art Gallery variant where each point of a polygon must be seen by k guards, and guards cannot see through other guards. Surprisingly, even covering convex polygons under this variant is not straightforward. For example, covering every point in a triangle k=4 times (a 4-cover) requires 5 guards, and achieving a 10-cover requires 12 guards. Our main result is tight bounds on k-covering a convex polygon of n vertices, for all k and n. The proofs of both upper and lower bounds are nontrivial. We also obtain bounds for simple polygons, leaving tight bounds an open problem.

entries.name: The Kähler-Ricci soliton on bounded pseudoconvex domains
entries.abstract: In this paper, we establish rigidity results for Kähler--Ricci solitons on bounded pseudoconvex domains in $\mathbb C^n$. We first show that if a complete Kähler metric has $C^1$ quasi-bounded geometry and negatively pinched Ricci curvature outside a compact set, then any soliton vector field whose metric dual is closed must vanish. In particular, such a soliton is Kähler--Einstein. We then prove that any Bergman Kähler--Ricci soliton of bounded domains is Kähler--Einstein. Combined with Huang--Xiao's resolution of Cheng's conjecture, this yields a soliton analogue of Cheng's conjecture. We also provide several model domains as examples.

entries.name: The Sample Complexity of Distributed Simple Binary Hypothesis Testing under Information Constraints
entries.abstract: This paper resolves two open problems from a recent paper, arXiv:2403.16981, concerning the sample complexity of distributed simple binary hypothesis testing under information constraints. The first open problem asks whether interaction reduces the sample complexity of distributed simple binary hypothesis testing. In this paper, we show that sequential interaction does not help. The second problem suggests tightening existing sample complexity bounds for communication-constrained simple binary hypothesis testing. We derive optimally tight bounds for this setting and resolve this problem. Our main technical contributions are: (i) a one-shot lower bound on the Bayes error in simple binary hypothesis testing that satisfies a crucial tensorisation property; (ii) a streamlined proof of the formula for the sample complexity of simple binary hypothesis testing without constraints, first established in arXiv:2403.16981; and (iii) a reverse data-processing inequality for Hellinger-$λ$ divergences, generalising the results from arXiv:1812.03031 and arXiv:2206.02765.

entries.name: Nonuniqueness of Leray-Hopf solutions to the unforced incompressible 3D Navier-Stokes Equation
entries.abstract: The nonuniqueness of Leray-Hopf solutions to the unforced incompressible 3D Navier-Stokes equations is one of the central open problems in mathematical fluid dynamics. In this paper, we provide, to our knowledge, the first rigorous computer-assisted proof demonstrating such nonuniqueness. Inspired by earlier works in this area, we construct a Leray-Hopf solution in the self-similar setting and then establish the existence of a second solution by analyzing the stability of the linearized operator around this profile, showing that it corresponds to an unstable perturbation. To achieve this, we develop an innovative numerical method that computes candidate solutions with high precision and propose a framework for rigorously establishing exact solutions in a neighborhood of these candidates. A key step is to decompose the linearized operator into a coercive part plus a compact perturbation, which is further approximated by a finite-rank operator up to a small error. The invertibility of the linearized operator restricted to the image of this finite-rank approximation is then rigorously verified using computer-assisted proofs. This certifies the existence of an unstable eigenpair and, consequently, yields a second solution - indeed, infinitely many Leray-Hopf solutions.

entries.name: On min-Storey estimators for multiple testing and conformal novelty detection
entries.abstract: In a multiple testing task, finding an appropriate estimator of the proportion $π_0$ of non-signal in the data to boost power of false discovery rate (FDR) controlling procedures is a long-standing research theme, sometimes referred to as 'adaptive FDR control'. The interest in this theme has been reinforced in the recent years with conformal novelty detection, for which it turns out that similar tools can be used in combination with any 'blackbox' machine learning algorithm. Nevertheless, perhaps surprisingly, finding a solution for 'adaptive FDR control' that is optimal in a broad sense is still an open problem. This paper fills this gap by introducing new $π_0$-estimators, referred to as min-Storey (MS) and interval-min-Storey (IMS), which are built upon the so-called 'Storey estimator'. Plugging these estimators in the adaptive Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure is shown to deliver FDR control both in the independent and conformal settings. In addition, these methods satisfy an optimal power property over any (regular) alternative distribution. The excellent behaviors of the new adaptive procedures are illustrated with numerical experiments both in the independent and conformal models for various distribution structures.

entries.name: Homotopy exponents of polyhedral products
entries.abstract: We study Moore's conjecture and homotopy exponents for polyhedral products. For $(\underline{CA},\underline{A})^K$ where each $A_i$ is finite and has torsion-free homology, we prove that if $(\underline{CA},\underline{A})^K$ is rationally hyperbolic, then it has no homotopy exponent at any odd prime. Under the additional hypothesis $ΣA_i$ is homotopy equivalent to a finite-type wedge of simply-connected spheres, we show Moore's conjecture holds for $(\underline{CA},\underline{A})^K$. We also give criteria such that, for a large family of polyhedral join products, the associated polyhedral products are rationally hyperbolic, mod-$p^r$ hyperbolic for all but finitely many primes, and have no homotopy exponent at all but finitely many primes.

entries.name: The inducibility of 6-vertex graphs
entries.abstract: The inducibility constant $λ_{F}$ of a graph $F$ is the asymptotically maximum induced density of $F$ in a growing sequence of graphs. This paper systematically investigates the case when $F$ has 6 vertices (and there are 78 cases to consider up to isomorphism and complementation). We show that flag algebras can compute the sharp upper bound on $λ_F$ in 36 cases of which, as far as the authors know, 30 are new results. In each of the solved cases, we also prove results about the structure of large (almost) extremal graphs. In particular, we establish perfect stability in all 32 cases when the extremal construction has no quasirandom parts. We also present conjectures about the value of $λ_{F}$ for 12 further cases (where the upper and lower bounds are very close to each other).

entries.name: On some geometrization of compact metric spaces: A solution to the Banach-Ulam conjecture
entries.abstract: We propose a geometrization of compact metric spaces that is based on ideas of S. Banach and J. Mycielski. Then we prove the following conjecture of S. Banach and S. Ulam from 1935: in every compact metric space there exists a finitely additive probability measure, invariant under congruences. Moreover, our techniques allow us to solve a problem of M. Talagrand related to the Marczewski problem and the Banach-Tarski paradox with pieces having the property of Baire. We give also a very simple proof of the conjecture of Ulam about the product Lebesgue measure in the Hilbert cube and explain the existing results about congruence-invariant Borel measures in the language of our geometrization.

entries.name: Double-Scaling Limits for Monitored Haar Products
entries.abstract: We study products of independent Haar matrices interspersed with a fixed corank-one projection. As the matrix dimension $N$ and product length $L$ grow with $L/N\toτ$, we prove that the empirical distribution of squared singular values converges to the free multiplicative Poisson law with $S$-transform $S(z)=\exp(τ/(1+z))$, for both the unitary and orthogonal ensembles. Lagrange inversion yields its moments explicitly, proving Beenakker's conjectured Erlang formula for every moment order.

entries.name: Counting Near-Spanning Matchings in Latin Squares and Steiner Triple Systems
entries.abstract: Montgomery proved that for sufficiently large $n$, every Latin square of order $n$ has a partial transversal with $n-1$ cells, and every Steiner triple system of order $n$ has a matching with $\lfloor n/3\rfloor-1$ edges, thus confirming the Ryser-Brualdi-Stein conjecture for even $n$ and the conjecture of Brouwer. We prove sharp enumerative refinements of these results: there is an absolute constant $c>0$ such that, for sufficiently large $n$, (1) every Latin square of order $n$ has $ \left((1\pm n^{-c})\frac{n}{\mathrm {e}^2}\right)^n$ partial transversals with $n-1$ cells; (2) every Steiner triple system of order $n$ has $ \left((1\pm n^{-c})\frac{n}{2\mathrm {e}^2}\right)^{\lfloor n/3\rfloor}$ matchings with $\lfloor n/3\rfloor-1$ edges. The first estimate confirms predictions of Montgomery and Kelly. We also provide sharp estimates for the numbers of partial transversals and matchings of every smaller size.

entries.name: Boolean threshold functions, neuron capacity, and memory retrieval
